ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the perpendicular bisector $OM$ of side $AB$ intersects with the perpendicular bisector $ON$ of side $AC$ at point $O$. These two perpendicular bisectors respectively intersect $BC$ at points $D$ and $E$. Given $\angle ABC=30^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DAE$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ABC=30^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=40^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle ABC-\angle ACB=180^\circ-30^\circ-40^\circ=110^\circ$, \\
Since $DM$ is the perpendicular bisector of segment $AB$, \\
it follows that $DA=DB$, \\
Therefore, $\angle DAB=\angle ABC=30^\circ$, \\
Similarly, $EA=EC$, \\
Therefore, $\angle EAC=\angle ACB=40^\circ$, \\
Therefore, $\angle DAE=\angle BAC-\angle BAD-\angle EAC=110^\circ-30^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$;

Therefore, $\angle DAE = \angle BAC - \angle BAD - \angle EAC = 110^\circ - 30^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{40^\circ}$.
